texts.en:
Greetings, star travelers. We are the Curators.

Our ancient order was established eons ago by the various galactic powers in ascendancy at the time. We were dedicated towards the preservation of all knowledge, in an effort to safeguard the galaxy from descending into yet another dark age of mass extinctions and barbarism.

We failed.

Few of us remain today, but we are no less committed to our sacred mission than our predecessors were. We are willing to share some of our knowledge with you... for a price.

texts.en: Well met, explorers. You are speaking to the [curator_enclave_country.GetName]. Perhaps you are already familiar with the tenets of our ancient order. Like our esteemed colleagues in the other Curator enclaves, we are willing to trade provided that you can meet our rates.

texts.en: Perhaps you are wondering about the significance of the shapes you see on the mural behind me. That is a good question with a very interesting answer! The fee for this information is 15 quadrillion energy credits.

texts.zh: 我们是策展人，欢迎你们，请问你们需要什么服务？
texts.en: You have reached the Curators. How may we assist you?

texts.zh: 你们知不知道这次对话正在被七个来自不同领域的亚空间实体所密切地监听着？唉，想和他们交流是不可能的，因为你们的文明远不具备能与他们交流的通讯技术。
texts.en: Did you know that this conversation is being closely monitored by entities from seven different subspace realms? Alas, I fear that the technology to communicate with them is too far beyond the present capabilities of your civilization to do you any good.

texts.zh: 不用担心，我们已经更新了档案系统，[Root.GetName]的信息已经被记入了档案以供后辈们查阅。即使在你的帝国经历不可避免的消亡后，你们仍将在档案中被铭记。
texts.en: Fear not. We have updated our archives with information about the [Root.GetName] for future generations. You will be remembered long after the inevitable collapse of your star nation.

texts.zh: 我想告诉你的东西有很多，但我不能白白免费地告诉你。这个空间站需要很多能源来维持运转…我们必须考虑收支的平衡。
texts.en: There is so much I wish I could tell you, but I simply can't do it for free. This space station requires a lot of energy to operate... we must consider our overhead.

texts.zh: 谨代表策展人协会向您问候，请问您有什么需要的吗？
texts.en: Greetings on behalf of the Curator order. Was there something you wanted?

texts.zh: 我们一向很高兴能和你们的政府进行贸易，我们这里还有一些科技资源，你们有兴趣吗？
texts.en: As always, it is a pleasure doing business with your government. Can we interest you in some technology?

texts.zh: 很高兴见到你。我很肯定今天我们可以达成一些互利互惠的协定。
texts.en: It is good to see you. I am sure we can come to some sort of mutually beneficial agreement before this day is over.

texts.zh: 知识一旦落入了恶毒之徒的手中，就会变得相当危险。但我们能怎么办呢？毕竟我们需要能源才能运营下去……
texts.en: Knowledge in the wrong gripping appendages can be dangerous, but what can we do? We need energy to keep the lights on...

texts.zh: [Root.GetSpeciesName]，你们不知道的事情还有很多。求求你……让我们教授你们更多有关这个宇宙的知识吧。
texts.en: There is much that you do not yet know, [Root.GetSpeciesName]. Please... let us educate you about the universe.

texts.zh: 以太龙族这个物种并不适合在我们的宇宙中生存，最后的这只龙虽然很强，但也不是无敌的。
texts.en: The Ether Drake species is ill-suited to life in our universe. The last dragon is strong, but not invincible.

label.zh: 这东西到底是什么玩意？
label.en: What is it, really?

responses.zh:
传说中，以太巨龙的出现先于任何一个宇宙文明。它们曾经数量众多，但随着时代更迭他们的族群也在逐渐衰落。

可以说，此时此地并不适合它们的生存。它们似乎不大适应宇宙的物理法则，就好像它们是从其他的现实中进化而来一般。而这，正是事实所在。我们认为它们是来自一个我们宇宙开始之前就已终结的宇宙，也就是某次"大坍缩"中唯一的生还者。

离这里不远的那条龙恐怕是这个星系，乃至这个宇宙中最后的以太巨龙了。
responses.en:
By all accounts, the Ether Drakes predate all galactic civilization. There once were multitudes, but their race has been wasting away for eons.

They are ill-suited to life, here and now. Something about the physical laws of the universe does not agree with them, like they evolved in another reality. They did, in fact. We believe that they are but the last dregs of a universe that ended before ours began, the sole survivors of some "big crunch."

The dragon not far from here is the last of its kind in the galaxy, perhaps the universe.

label.zh: 告诉我们如何才能击败它。
label.en: Tell us how to defeat it.

responses.zh:
龙身上的鳞片对敲击节律有反应，更精确地说，特定的频率对它的皮下组织有着放松的作用，而那里控制着它们的用以移动与防护冲击的鳞片。这个条件反射曾是以太巨龙之间社交行为的关键环节，现在则成为了它的死穴。

调整舰船火力平台的攻击节奏到一个特定的频率，可以有效地增加以太巨龙所受到的伤害。它并不是主动想生存在这个世界之中——一劳永逸地结束它的痛苦吧。
responses.en:
Its scales respond to percussive rhythms. To be more precise, certain frequencies have a relaxing effect on the sub-dermal musculature controlling the positioning and shock absorption of their scale plates. A reflex that once played a key role in Ether Drake social interactions, it is now a clear and obvious weakness.

Adjusting the firing pattern of your vessels according to a particular rhythm will greatly increase the damage you can inflict on the last dragon. It was never meant for our age - put it out of its misery.

label.zh: 我们的舰队面对它该如何作战？
label.en: How would our current fleet fare against it in battle?

responses.zh:
你的舰队差劲，太差劲。

等等，难不成你想要去……我的天哪，就用你的这丁点舰队？那，那会变成一边倒的屠杀。
responses.en:
Poorly. Very poorly.

Wait a second, you're not actually thinking of...? My goodness, with the ships you have? It... it would be a slaughter!

label.zh: 我们的舰队面对它该如何作战？

responses.zh: 我强烈不建议你进行作战。你的攻击与其说是威胁它，更像是无谓的吵闹。
responses.en: I would strongly advise against it. Your attacks would likely be more of an annoyance than a threat.

label.zh: 我们的舰队面对它该如何作战？
label.en: How would our current fleet fare against it in battle?

responses.zh: 嗯……没错……没错，我想事实上你还是有很大的机会的。如果你联合你的整个舰队的话……我提醒你这场胜利不会轻松，但是起码你有胜利的可能性。
responses.en: Hmmm, yes... Yes, I suppose you might actually stand a chance. If you combined your entire fleet... It would not be an easy victory, mind you, but one that is at least within the realm of possibility.

label.zh: 我们的舰队面对它该如何作战？
label.en: How would our current fleet fare against it in battle?

responses.zh: 你的舰队是一支强大的舰队，甚至比得上一些被我们策展人编年史记载着的最伟大的无敌舰队。胜利掌握在你的手中。
responses.en: Yours is a mighty fleet, comparable to some of the greatest armadas recorded in the annals of the Curator Order. Victory is certainly within your reach.

texts.zh: 这是一种已经没人会再建造的，异想天开，体型巨大且能自我维持的建筑。也许不建是明智的选择。
texts.en: It is the kind of absurd, massive and self-perpetuating construction that you don't see built anymore. Maybe that is for the best.

label.en: Any structure can be destroyed.

responses.zh: 这座堡垒曾经被击毁过，但它总能恢复原状。一些古老的帝国曾经因未能揭开它更深层次的秘密，抑或是未能永久地毁灭它而陷入癫狂。这座堡垒对于维持自身是如此尽心尽力，令人不得不怀疑它是否还有其他的正经用途。
responses.en: The Fortress has been defeated before, but it always recovers. Some of the ancient empires of this galaxy were driven to madness by their vain efforts to unlock its deeper secrets, or else to permanently destroy it. It appears so focused on maintaining itself that we doubt it has any other serious purpose.

label.en: Can the fortress be entered?

responses.zh: 可以，而且已经有人进入过了，尽管那项尝试的壮举已经在时间的流逝中几乎被忘却。这座堡垒在关闭状态时仅能维持部分供能，不过它会尝试从附近摄取能量以迅速重启系统。请务必小心。
responses.en: It can and it has been, although that attempt is now nearly forgotten. The fortress maintains only partial power while in shutdown, however it will attempt to draw power from nearby sources in order to jump-start its systems again. Proceed with caution.

label.zh: 重新给我们讲讲如何进入该建筑。
label.en: Remind us about entering it.

responses.zh: 可以，而且已经有人进入过了，尽管那项尝试的壮举已经在时间的流逝中几乎被忘却。这座堡垒在关闭状态时仅能维持部分供能，不过它会尝试从附近摄取能量以迅速重启系统。请务必小心。
responses.en: It can and it has been, although that attempt is now nearly forgotten. The fortress maintains only partial power while in shutdown, however it will attempt to draw power from nearby sources in order to jump-start its systems again. Proceed with caution.

label.en: Who built the fortress?

responses.zh: 不管是谁，他们一定对于谜题与解密十分着迷。人们过去只从堡垒里面回收了一些形状奇怪的金属物件：这些古怪装置的零件，似乎设计上可以通过重新排列组成更加自然的形态。当时的回收人员并未能解开谜题，但所幸从堡垒中死里逃生。绝大多数人就没能活着出来了。
responses.en: Whoever they were, they must have been fond of puzzles and enigmas. The only items to have been recovered from the fortress are strange metal shapes: components of perplexing contraptions which seem designed to be rearranged into more satisfying forms. Those who brought them back did so because they failed, and they barely escaped with their lives. Many others didn't.

label.zh: 重新给我们讲讲该建筑的建造者。
label.en: Remind us who built it.

responses.zh: 不管是谁，他们一定对于谜题与解密十分着迷。人们过去只从堡垒里面回收了一些形状奇怪的金属物件：这些古怪装置的零件，似乎设计上可以通过重新排列组成更加自然的形态。当时的回收人员并未能解开谜题，但所幸从堡垒中死里逃生。绝大多数人就没能活着出来了。
responses.en: Whoever they were, they must have been fond of puzzles and enigmas. The only items to have been recovered from the fortress are strange metal shapes: components of perplexing contraptions which seem designed to be rearranged into more satisfying forms. Those who brought them back did so because they failed, and they barely escaped with their lives. Many others didn't.

label.en: How is the fortress powered?

responses.zh:
动力系统一定是在建造最初舱体与安装防御系统之间的某个时候建造而成的。我们尚不清楚它的恢复方式，但我们发现堡垒中保存着巨量的暗物质。了解那些物质与以及其与黑洞的关系，是弄清堡垒长久以来运作方式的关键。

没人曾经成功找到它的动力源，但这动力的来源似乎十分不稳定。
responses.en:
The power system must have been built at a time between initial construction of the hull, and installation of its defense systems. The system's recovery method is unknown to us, but we have discovered that the fortress contains large quantities of dark matter. That substance and its relationship to black holes are key to understanding how the fortress has lasted so long.

No one has ever found the source of its power, but it is likely to be extremely volatile.

label.zh: 重新给我们讲讲该建筑的供能方式。
label.en: Remind us how it is powered.

responses.zh:

The power system must have been built at a time between initial construction of the hull, and installation of its defense systems. The system's recovery method is unknown to us, but we have discovered that the fortress contains large quantities of dark matter. That substance and its relationship to black holes are key to understanding how the fortress has lasted so long.

No one has ever found the source of its power, but it is likely to be extremely volatile.

texts.en: The Stellar Devourer is a new parasite on the galactic hunting ground, not unlike your empire in many ways. It was born out of fear and nuclear fusion. It roams the galaxy, submerging itself into stars, feasting on them from within. And it certainly does not like being disturbed.

label.zh: 这东西到底是什么玩意？
label.en: What is it, really?

这种恒星吞噬者是一种很罕见的生物，我们并不知道这种怪物的来源。我们手上现有的情报非常有限，只有极少数的情报提供源获得了与它们接触的第一手资料。

但是我们现有的资料都指向了一个事实：这是一种极其可怕的生物，它只会带来毁灭。

噬星者能够以聚变为食。我们得出了一个非常有说服力的推断：它是暗物质和恒星物质在外部维度层面上融合的产物。它们潜进恒星内部，吞噬其中的物质来为其内部聚变反应堆提供燃料。它所到的恒星系，无一逃得过灭亡的命运。在它的盛宴之后，行星们要么像冰一样粉碎，要么暴露在它胃中的第二太阳之下被烧尽。

它贪得无厌，永远不会停下吞噬的脚步。当你注视着它的时候，你会从中看到为了生存而透露出的无以言表的狂怒。

The star-feaster is a rare breed. A new type of beast of unknown origin. The accounts we have collected are few and sparse with intel. Few sources even have firsthand experience with the thing.

All our data points to the same fact, however: it is a terror that brings nothing but ruin.

The Stellar Devourer is capable of feeding off of fusion itself. Our very educated guess is that its biology is the result of some outer-dimensional fusing of dark matter and solar matter. It dives into stars, feasting on their innards in order to fuel its own, internal fusion reactor. It brings death to all systems it reaches. Either they shatter like ice after its banquet, or they burn from being exposed to a second sun from within the being's belly.

It wants to feed, and it will stop at nothing to get its share. When you gaze at it, what you see is a survivor's raw fury.

label.en: Tell us how to defeat it.

responses.zh:
我们目前唯一确定的事实是，噬星者最重要的部分是它的集成核心。它极度需要维持其内部的反应炉运转，避免让寒冷的虚空接触到它内部使其自行崩塌。没有那些恒星物质，它就没办法存活。

这是一个你们可以利用的缺陷。你们可以将武器按照我们提供的标准来进行校准，这样你们就能穿破保护其消化系统的外层组织。打伤它，你就能看到它的内部物质喷射出来，扩散到整个星系。

The only thing we know for sure is that the collected core is the most important aspect of the Stellar Devourer. The creature desperately needs to keep its furnace burning, lest the cold void of space reaches its vital organs deeper within and makes it collapse in on itself. Without that stellar matter, it is nothing.

You can use this to your advantage. Calibrate your weapons to our specifications and you can then home in on the very membranes that hold the Devourer's digestive system together. Wound it and you will see its innards gush out across the solar system.

所幸，它没能完全转移至我们的宇宙。如若不然，它可能早已经将所有的生命赶尽杀绝了。

It is a creature of pure malice, born in a dimension that bears more than a striking resemblance to the realm of Hell as described by many galactic religions. What we are seeing is but a small part of a greater whole - the creature in its entirety is multitudes larger.

It is very fortunate that it was unable to complete its transition into our universe. Had it been successful, the creature would likely have consumed all life in the galaxy by now.

尽管流传着许多谣言，目前没有任何证据表明它们具备任何智慧生物的特征。它们喜欢在小行星里筑巢，并且攻击所有它们认为是有威胁的东西。
responses.en:
They are an aggressively territorial silicon-based life form. Although they once posed a significant threat to spacefaring civilizations, their numbers have been severely culled over the last 500,000 years and the surviving members of their species are fairly reclusive.

Despite rumors to the contrary, there is no evidence that they possess anything that could be described as sapient intelligence. They tend to nest inside asteroids, and they will attack anything which is perceived as a threat.

texts.en:
Ah yes, the chromatic being from long ago. We have studied it for as long as our order has existed. As have several civilizations before us.

This machine is beyond ancient. For all we know, it has always been. And yet, all it does is orbit that black hole. It's fascinating to us, but we understand if it is too much for you to grasp.

responses.zh: 你口中笼统称为无限神机的存在，是无法进行回收的，更无法获得它的任何信息。整个星系中没有任何一个骇客或者工程师能透过它闪亮的外壳看到里面的任何东西——我们很清楚它里面藏着许多有价值的信息。我们也束手无策。我们既不知道它的用途，也不知道它接下去的任务是什么。
responses.en: The Infinity Machine, as you so bluntly call it, is impervious to extraction. No information comes out from it. No hacker or engineer in the entire galaxy has been able to see through its shiny exterior to gain a glimpse of the knowledge it so obviously withholds from us. We are at a loss. We neither know what it is for, nor what it aims to do once it's done.

label.zh: 告诉我们如何才能击败它。
label.en: Tell us how to defeat it.

responses.zh:
有一种办法大概可以摧毁它。我们虽然无法从它身上获得任何信息，但它的外壳还是可以破坏的。采矿者曾经无数次尝试过从它上面获取资源，但回来时全都狼狈不堪。不过他们发现了一些有趣的情况：无限神机并不像看起来那样坚不可摧。

它是由一种能够调节其自身属性的材料构成。密度、弹性、温度，只有你想不到，没有它变不了的！它能够实时分析伤害，并及时改变外壳特性进行补偿。这样一来，外界的伤害就很难摧毁它了。你要做的，就是改变攻击的频率，调整导弹的热力输出，不管用什么攻击方式，想方设法地进行变化。这样你们才能克服无限神机外壳的适应性。

Miners have tried to gather resources from it at numerous times, only to come back with their ships barely holding together. But they did find something interesting: The Infinity Machine is not as rigid as it seems.

It is made of a material capable of changing its characteristics. Density, flexibility, heat, you name it! It can analyze damage in real time and change its shell to compensate, thus making itself harder to take down. Change your frequencies, adjust the thermal output of your missiles, whatever you people lumber around with, and keep changing them. That way you can get past its adaptive capabilities.

texts.en: A sad story. Its masters have been dead for millions of years, but this massive warship continues to stand vigil over the broken rubble of their empire.

label.zh: 这东西到底是什么玩意？
label.en: What is it, really?

七百万年前，曾经有个伟大的星际帝国在我们的星系中一个不起眼的地方兴盛强大，这是那曾经无比强大的帝国的旗舰之一。历史往往都是相似的，这个帝国在一系列与邻国的惨烈战争中骤然消亡。

你遇到的无畏战舰是他们最后的遗物。尽管船员们都已经去世，电脑系统还在尽职地巡逻。在这段漫长的时光中，无数人都曾想让这艘战舰安息——但没有一次成功。
responses.en:
It was one of several flagships belonging to an unusually powerful interstellar empire that flourished in a small region of our galaxy some seven million years ago. As is so often the case, that empire was brought to a sudden and violent end at the hands of its neighbors in a series of very destructive wars.

The dreadnought you have encountered is the last of its kind, and it continues to dutifully patrol its assigned system despite the death of its crew. Many attempts have been made throughout the ages to put the old warship to its final rest - none successful.

texts.zh: 神出鬼没的幽魂是一种令人烦躁的生物，如果它们能被称为生物的话。我们把它们当做是一种罕见但是极具破坏力的自然灾害。
texts.en: Spectral Wraiths are disturbing creatures, if they are creatures at all. We consider them a rare and extraordinarily efficient natural disaster.

label.zh: 你对这种灾害有什么了解？
label.en: What do you know about these disasters?

responses.zh:
它们似乎像是光影形成的幻象，但等你凑近去看，马上就会发现它们与幻象相去甚远。

打倒它们的关键就在于它们的形态，虽然这听起来有些矛盾。可见光谱影响着它们的力量，当它们接近相似频率的光源时，力量就会减弱。时刻注意幽魂的颜色变化。
responses.en:
They appear to be illusions of light, but when you get close, it quickly grows apparent that they are far from illusory.

Paradoxically, in that appearance lies the key to their defeat. Their relationship with the visible spectrum of light is their strength, but it diminishes when they approach a light source of a similar frequency. Pay close attention to the color of the Wraith.

label.zh: 红色幽魂是什么样的呢？
label.en: What about red Wraiths?

responses.zh: 红色幽魂的频率是450THz。它们的光与M级恒星是一致的。它们免疫传统武器攻击的能力在有红矮星的恒星系里将会被削弱。
responses.en: Red Wraiths have a frequency of 450THz. Their light is synchronized with that of a Class M Star. Their ability to avoid conventional weaponry is weakened in systems with red dwarfs.

texts.zh: 如果我们没猜错的话，虚空孳孽来自很远的地方。我们认为它是某种巨大无比的星系际捕食者的后代，他们会在虚空中寻找猎物。尽管我们从未遭遇过活的个体，我们听说过虚空孳孽的成年体所过之处，皆是破坏与混乱的故事。据说星球会在它们的阴影下溃烂。
texts.en: If our suspicions hold true, the Voidspawn is far away from home. We believe it is the progeny of an extragalactic predator of unthinkable proportions: one that stalks the void of space in search of its prey. Though we have never before encountered a live specimen, we have heard tales of the destruction and chaos grown Voidspawn leave in their wake. It is said that worlds fester under their shadow.

label.zh: 这东西到底是什么玩意？
label.en: What is it, really?

responses.zh:
据我们所知，母体会在恒星的轨道上产下星球大小的蛋，并花费数千年来孵化，有时甚至久到足以在蛋壳上发展出大气层与有机生命。

它们以活体物质为食，而成年虚空孳孽据说会对所有活物造成一种奇怪的影响。幸运的是，这只幼体似乎被其父母抛弃了。

或许我们最好该趁它尚未成熟之时将它消灭？
responses.en:
From what we can tell, the mother lays its planet-sized eggs in orbit of a star, where they then incubate for thousands of years, sometimes even long enough to develop an atmosphere and organic life.

They feed off of living matter, and adult Voidspawn are said to exert a strange influence on all living things. Fortunately this spawn seems to have been abandoned by its parents.

Perhaps it would be best to stifle the creature while it is still young and vulnerable?

label.en: How is it defeated?

responses.zh: 我们从未听说有谁曾击败过成年虚空孳孽，但这只才刚刚出生。虚空孳孽会喷出腐蚀性的黏液和尖刺，连最厚的装甲都可以烧穿，但涂上一层抗酸涂层可以减缓这一过程。我们会为你们提供帮助。虚空孳孽对我们所有人都是个威胁。
responses.en: We have never heard of a grown Voidspawn being defeated in battle, but this one is newly hatched. The Voidspawn projects corrosive spittle and spikes that can burn through the thickest of armor, but applying a protective acid-proof coating may slow its progress. We will help you make it. The Voidspawn is a threat to us all.

texts.zh:
啊，废品机器人。拾荒者是一个失落时代的奇特造物。它无止尽地在残骸场中搜寻，将从无数残骸中搜获的枪炮，引擎，材料焊至自己的外壳上。其体量与火力数百年以来一直以这种方式提升，而且毫不减缓。

如果有足够的时间与废品，没有人知道它到底能将自己造得多大。
texts.en:
Ah, the scrap bot. The Scavenger is a curious construct from a lost age. Endlessly it searches through the debris fields of the galaxy, welding the guns, engines, and materials scavenged from countless derelicts onto its own hull. Its mass and firepower have been increasing in such a fashion for centuries, with no sign of relenting.

No-one knows if there is an upper limit to how massive it could become, given enough time and scrap to work with.

label.en: Who built it, initially?

responses.zh:
不幸的是，关于拾荒者的起源并没有准确的数据。有些科学家认为它是一个失落帝国的废品回收机器人，但出了故障，其原本用途早已被硬件劣化埋没了。也有人认为它原本是一个微小的纳米机器人，在其程序驱动下，利用其周围环境来不断地使自己变大变强。还有人认为它当初是机器人舰长，是数千年前一场星际大战的唯一幸存者。因其文明突然且彻底的毁灭，导致其逻辑系统无法挽回地受损了。

当然，这些都只是猜测。
responses.en:
Unfortunately, no definitive data regarding the Scavenger's origin is known to exist. Some researchers believe it to be a malfunctioning scrap collection service machine from a lost empire, its purpose long since muddled by hardware degradation. Others believe it to have originated as a single microscopic nanobot, programmed to endlessly build itself larger and stronger by exploiting its environment. Still others reckon it may have started out as a robotic ship's captain; the sole survivor of an intergalactic battle waged millennia ago. Perhaps its reasoning systems were irrevocably damaged by the sudden destruction of its entire civilization.

Of course, this is all just speculation.

label.en: Who built it, initially?

label.zh: 再给我们讲讲它的起源。
label.en: Remind us about its origins.
Can we communicate with it?

responses.zh:
多年来许多人都试图与拾荒机器人沟通，或者转而尝试更改其程序。不幸的是，这些远征队大多数都变成了拾荒者机器人身处的宇宙垃圾场的一部分。只有那些跑得比它还快的才活了下来。

它身上焊接的重炮火力已经足以单枪匹马消灭整个帝国的舰队——而且这样的情况可能已经发生过不止一次了。当然，这种毁灭性的遭遇只会进一步增强拾荒者，为其提供更多可利用的舰船部件。
responses.en:
Over the years there have been many attempts to communicate with it, or else to alter the programming of the Scavenger. Unfortunately, most of those expeditions ended up part of the cosmic scrap yards where the Scavenger Bot dwells. Only those who were able to outrun it survived.

The Scavenger has welded enough heavy artillery onto its patchwork frame to single-handedly destroy an entire nation's fleet - an event that may already have occurred on more than one occasion. Of course, any such destructive encounters would only have served to further strengthen the Scavenger, providing it with more ship components to repurpose.

label.en: Can we communicate with it?

label.zh: 再给我们讲讲与它沟通的尝试。
label.en: Remind us about attempts at communicating with it.

label.zh: 告诉我们如何才能击败它。
label.en: Tell us how to defeat it.

responses.zh:
你可能已经推测到了：拾荒者并非按照任何明确的现成图纸而造。因此，它的某些部件并不太……合身，导致了一些不连续的结构弱点。当然，外行人一眼看不出这些弱点，但我们的先进传感器已经设法确定了它们的位置。

让你的舰队集中火力攻击我们在拾荒者上标明的这些部位，应该可以大幅降低击溃它所需要倾斜的火力。
responses.en:
As you may have surmised: the Scavenger was not built according to any definitive, pre-existing schematics. As a result, some of its parts fit together... less than optimally, leading to a discrete number of structural weaknesses. Of course, to the uninitiated, most of these are obscured from view - but our advanced sensors have managed to isolate them.

Tell your fleets to focus fire on the indicated sections of the Scavenger's hull, and it should substantially reduce the amount of damage the construct is able to take before collapsing.

texts.zh: 真壮观，不是吗？一只消瘦的老族母，她的外皮在漫漫岁月中变白变硬，战列舰在她的触手中就像牡蛎壳一般脆弱。几十年前，我们的科学家听说有一位舰长，发誓要狩猎族母至星系尽头。不过，考虑到族母仍然存活，我们可以肯定他未能成功。
texts.en: Magnificent, is she not? A wizened old Matriarch, her hide bleached and hardened by the eons, her tentacles capable of snapping the hulls of battleships like oyster shells. Decades ago, our researchers heard rumors of a captain sworn to hunt the Matriarch to the ends of the galaxy. However, considering her continued existence, we cannot imagine he met with success.

label.zh: 为什么族母比其它缇扬奇要大许多？
label.en: Why is the Matriarch so much larger than other Tiyanki?

responses.zh:
她惊人的巨大身躯实属异常。我们认为族母是来自另一星系的漂流者，那里的缇扬奇与我们星系中的缇扬奇进化产生了分歧，变得更大更强。

当然，另一种可能性是族母只是得了一种巨大畸形症——不过这无法解释她的长寿。
responses.en:
Her incredible size is an anomaly, to be sure. We believe the Matriarch is a wanderer from another galaxy in deep space, where a species of Tiyanki far greater in size and strength diverged evolutionarily from the Tiyanki found in our own.

Of course, it is also possible the Matriarch is simply suffering from an advanced form of gigantism - though this would fail to explain her extended lifespan.

label.zh: 再给我们讲讲为何族母比其它缇扬奇要大许多。
label.en: Remind us why the Matriarch is larger than other Tiyanki.

label.en: What do you know about the captain hunting the Matriarch?

responses.zh: 很少。那位舰长很可能从另一个星系追着族母来到了这里。不过，为何有人会蠢到挑战可以单枪匹马消灭整支舰队的生物仍是个谜。
responses.en: Very little. It is quite possible the captain chased the Matriarch here from another galaxy. Though why one would be foolish enough to challenge a creature capable of destroying entire fleets with just one vessel is beyond us.

label.en: Remind us about the captain hunting the Matriarch.

label.zh: 告诉我们如何才能击败它。
label.en: Tell us how to defeat it.

responses.zh:
族母非常强大，但并非坚不可摧。尽管她的装甲外壳可以抵御多种投射物，她仍有一个可观的弱点。

在她的背上插着一枚巨型质子鱼雷，这是最近一场战斗中留下的仍未愈合的伤口。尽管那颗鱼雷似乎故障了，我们的扫描显示它仍可以引爆，只要用一道特定的能源脉冲诱发即可。

我们现在将详情发送给你。
responses.en:
The Matriarch is formidable, but not indestructible. While her armored hide protects her from a wide range of projectiles, she carries with her a remarkable weakness.

There is a massive proton torpedo lodged in her back: a wound from a recent battle that has healed poorly. While seemingly defective, our scans of the torpedo suggest it can still be detonated, if agitated with a specific energy pulse.

We will transmit the details to you now.

texts.en: The Toxic Entity is an elusive being. It has roamed the galaxy for millennia, occasionally choosing to spurt venom at worlds in what we can only imagine is a natural stage of its life cycle. We have heard that it has been tracked to the [toxic_god_system.GetName] system.

texts.zh:
毒性神祗是一个捉摸不透的存在。几千年来它在星系内来回游荡，偶尔会选择某个星球喷洒毒液——我们只能猜测这是其生命循环的某个自然阶段。当然，你肯定早就知道了！

我们很抱歉，但是我们没法帮你找到它现在所在的位置——我们的全体线人都有好一阵子没看到它了。
texts.en:
The Toxic Entity is an elusive being. It has roamed the galaxy for millennia, occasionally choosing to spurt venom at worlds in what we can only imagine is a natural stage of its life cycle. But you already knew this, of course!

We are sorry, but we cannot help you find its present whereabouts - it has not been spotted by any of our contacts for quite some time.

label.zh: 这东西到底是什么玩意？
label.en: What is it, really?

responses.zh: 没有文献记载毒性神祗究竟从何而来。第一次目击是在数千年之前，自那以后每过几个世纪就有人目击过。某些人视其为神明，但具体如何得由你自己判断。我们能够告诉你的是，它是一个极度令人畏惧的有机生物，有着节肢动物的特征。有报告表明，它的体型相当巨大，上面甚至发展出了一整个生态系统。当然，获取其生物学样本的难度可以预想是有多么困难了。
responses.en: It is not documented where the Toxic Entity came from. The first sighting was several thousand years ago, and since then it has been seen every few centuries. Some have called it a deity, but that is for you to decide. What we can tell you is that it is an extremely formidable organic being with arthropoid characteristics. Reports suggest that it is sufficiently large that an entire ecosystem has developed on it, though acquiring samples of its biology has proved understandably challenging.

label.en: Knights of the Toxic God

responses.zh: 过去撞见它的人中有少数几个幸存者。根据报告，它带有腐蚀性的毒液能够烧蚀任何形态的装甲。护盾相对来说更加有用一丁点。此外，在它的背上生活的那些生物在剧毒实体受到威胁的时候，会像蜂群一样发动攻击。我们只能建议你带着压倒性的军力去接近它。
responses.en: There have been few survivors to its past encounters. According to reports, its corrosive poisons are able to burn through all forms of armor. Shields are only slightly more useful. Furthermore, the creatures living on its back will supposedly act as an attack swarm when it is threatened. We can only suggest you approach it with overwhelming force.

texts.zh: 那个颇为神经质的自动化机械体来到这个星系的时间并不长，但不要被这种新奇所迷惑。奥普斯哨兵的创造者们在被一台专横的机器同化之前，就已经是他们所在领域中最杰出的工程师之一。我们不知道自那时起，那个机器意识遭遇了怎样严酷的命运，但从哨兵那痛苦的扭动来看：情况似乎相当不稳定。如果你决定满足自己的好奇心，务必小心行事。
texts.en: That rather twitchy automaton is a relative newcomer to the galaxy, but don't be fooled by such novelty. The Opus Sentinel's creators were counted among the finest engineers in their sector even before they were assimilated by a tyrannical machine. We do not know what harsh fate has befallen the machine consciousness since then, but if the Sentinel's agonized writhing is anything to go by: the whole situation appears quite volatile. Tread carefully, should you decide to slake your curiosity.

texts.zh:
恕我冒昧，但我以为您会比我们更了解此事！与我们所研究的对象相比，那个颇为不安的自动化机械体是个新面孔，但作为对手同样令人畏惧。

我们知道，即便在被同化之前，奥普斯哨兵背后的工程师们也被认为是该领域最优秀的人才。因此，那艘战舰不容小觑。我们不太清楚的是，这艘船是如何与[origin_unplugged_assimilator_empire.GetName]如此疏远的。从“哨兵”痛苦的扭动来看，我们推测情况仍然相当不稳定。您是否同意这一评估，[root.GetSpeciesName]？
texts.en:
Forgive my impertinence, but I assumed you would know more about it than we do! That rather twitchy automaton is a newcomer compared to what we usually study here, but is no less fearsome an opponent.

We know that even before they were assimilated, the engineers behind the Opus Sentinel were counted among the finest in their sector. That warship is therefore not to be underestimated. What is less clear to us is how the vessel became so detached from the [origin_unplugged_assimilator_empire.GetName]. We gather from the Sentinel's agonized writhing that the whole situation remains quite volatile. Would you agree with assessment, [root.GetSpeciesName]?

label.zh: 你是说它在守护着什么吗？
label.en: You say it is guarding something?

responses.zh: 正是，尽管我们并不确切知道是什么。我们的一些联系人认为，哨兵正在保卫分裂的[origin_unplugged_assimilator_empire.GetName]所剩下的任何东西；另一些人则暗示，这颗星球本身蕴藏着某种宝藏。我们所知道的是，这艘战舰的建造比其[origin_unplugged_assimilator_empire.GetAdj]同类坚固得多，甚至高出一个数量级。无论它在保护什么，奥普斯哨兵都在坚持，尽管有明显的痛苦迹象，甚至可能是极度的煎熬。
responses.en: Indeed, though we do not know precisely what. Some of our contacts believe the Sentinel is defending whatever remains of the splintered [origin_unplugged_assimilator_empire.GetName]; others suggest the planet itself holds some treasure. What we do know is that this warship was built more robustly than any of its [origin_unplugged_assimilator_empire.GetAdj] peers by an order of magnitude. Whatever it is protecting out there, the Opus Sentinel perseveres despite clear signs of distress, or perhaps even agony.

label.en: We prefer not to talk about it.

responses.zh:
完全可以理解。我们只是出于好奇。

还有其他我可以帮您的吗？
responses.en:
Quite understandable. We are merely curious.

Is there anything else I can help you with?

responses.en:
Seeing as how you are one of our more trustworthy clients... I can tell you the Opus Sentinel was last seen guarding the [origin_unplugged_machine_legacy_core.GetName] system.

等等——别告诉我你就是[From.GetSpeciesNamePlural]？真是万分抱歉……我一定是把你跟……[unfriends.GetName]搞混了？

跟你讲，只要你告诉我们一件我们还不知道的，关于无限球体的事，我们就会慷慨地奖励你。
texts.en:
YOU!? Uncover the Infinity Machine's secret?! That is about as likely as the [From.GetSpeciesNamePlural] are to survive into the next century. Not very likely, if that was unclear.

Wait - don't tell me YOU are the [From.GetSpeciesNamePlural]? My sincerest apologies... I must have confused you with the... [unfriends.GetName]?

Tell you what: give us one thing we do not yet know about the Infinity Sphere and we will reward you handsomely.

label.en: Prepare to have your minds blown.

尽管你明显不知道自己的发现有多么重大，[Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural]，你来找我们是对的，对此我们表示感谢。
responses.en:
You cannot mean to say... But if the AI entered the Gargantua black hole it can only mean that... But it cannot, for if it were it would be beyond our comprehension...

Though the magnitude of your finds clearly eludes you [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural], you were right to come to us, and for this you have our gratitude.

它们为何不同？它们通往哪里？我们决定不要对这些谜团太过深究——“一朝被蛇咬，零点一七年怕井绳”这道理你懂的——但我们愿意分享一些可能与其有关的近期发现。

texts.en:
The L-Gates? Yes, like the other Gateways they predate even the oldest Stagnant Ascendancy, but we are sure you have figured that out already.

Why are they different? Where do they lead? We have opted not to delve too deeply into those particular mysteries - "thrice bitten, zero-point-seventeen shy" you know how it is - but we are willing to share some recent revelations that just might be related.

For a price.
